s51.definition: An outlier is an observation that lies far away from the rest of the data, so far that it looks like it was produced by a different mechanism.

causes.meaning: A value that was typed or measured wrongly, so it can never be true.
causes.here: 2011-03-10 has humidity 0 %, which is impossible outdoors. Fixed in Unit 1 (replaced by the mean of the neighbouring days).

causes.meaning: The instrument is right in general but imprecise on that reading.
causes.here: Not seen: the weather values are daily means from an official station and the rental counts are exact system logs.

causes.meaning: The observation comes from a different population than the rest.
causes.here: Not seen: every row is one day of the same bike system in the same city.

causes.meaning: An unusual but real day at the edge of normal behaviour.
causes.here: The 26-27 January 2011 snowstorm (431 and 506 rentals) and 26 December 2012, a rainy day after Christmas (441).

causes.meaning: A real event that changes the process for a day.
causes.here: Hurricane Sandy, 29 October 2012: 22 rentals on an 18 °C day. The lowest day in the data.

events.what: Hurricane Sandy hits the US east coast; the city shuts down

families.idea: Assume a distribution for one variable and flag values too far from its centre.
A point is an outlier if its nearest neighbours are far away.
families.threshold: No fixed rule: rank by score, look at the top

families.idea: A point is an outlier if its neighbourhood is much sparser than its neighbours' neighbourhoods.
families.far: LOF = average lrd of neighbours ÷ own lrd
families.threshold: No fixed rule: LOF ≈ 1 normal, LOF ≫ 1 outlier
